title: Simple forces including magnets (Year 3 unit)
desc: A 12-lesson online unit: surfaces and contact forces, magnetic force at a distance, the parts of magnets, magnetic and non-magnetic materials, attract or repel, and blocking magnetic force. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Do one lesson a day and have a fridge magnet and household objects nearby to test. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What are magnets?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson video introducing what magnets are, followed by quiz questions online.
how: A good first lesson before testing which things at home a magnet picks up.

title: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials
desc: Lesson on sorting materials into magnetic and non-magnetic. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Print the worksheet and let the child test real objects with a magnet before filling it in.

title: Putting magnets together: attract or repel
desc: Lesson on what happens when magnet poles meet: attract or repel. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Pair it with two bar or ring magnets so the child feels the push and pull.

title: Different magnets and their parts
desc: Lesson on the different shapes of magnets and their north and south poles. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Use before the attract-or-repel lesson.

title: Introduction to sound (Year 4 unit)
desc: A 12-lesson online unit on how sounds are made, how vibrations travel, vibrations in solids, volume, sound insulation and pitch. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Work through in order; many lessons suggest simple home tests with rubber bands, cups and string. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What is sound?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson: the child watches a video explaining that sound comes from vibrations, then answers a starter and exit quiz.
how: Let the child touch their throat while humming to feel the vibration.

title: How sounds are made (teacher lesson)
desc: Lesson showing that sounds are made when something vibrates, with demonstrations using a speaker, a small dish of water and a tuning fork.
how: Read the lesson plan for demo ideas; a steel spoon tapped near a bowl of water works instead of a tuning fork.

title: How vibrations travel
desc: Lesson on how sound vibrations travel through a medium to our ears. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Follow it with a string-and-cup telephone made at home.

title: What are the 5 senses?
desc: An Oak Year 1 pupil lesson video introducing the five senses, at the start of a unit on sound and hearing.
how: Afterwards play a blindfold guessing game using smell, touch and sound.

title: Simple electrical circuits (Year 4 unit)
desc: A 10-lesson online unit: electrical appliances, components of a circuit, building circuits, troubleshooting, switches, conductors and insulators, and working safely with electricity. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Pair with a cheap battery, bulb and wire kit; supervise and never use mains sockets. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What are circuit diagrams?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson where the child learns the symbols used to draw circuits, through a video and quizzes.
how: Ask the child to draw the circuit they built using the symbols.

title: What are insulators and conductors?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on which materials let electricity pass through (conductors) and which don't (insulators), with a video and quizzes.
how: Test a coin, a pencil lead, a plastic spoon and paper in a battery-and-bulb circuit.

title: Working with electricity
desc: The safety lesson in Oak's circuits unit, on using electricity safely. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Use it to talk through home rules about sockets, wet hands and broken wires.

title: Troubleshooting problems with circuits
desc: Lesson where children work out why a circuit doesn't work. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Give the child a deliberately broken circuit to fix.

title: Introduction to light and shadows (Year 3 unit)
desc: A 12-lesson online unit: light and seeing, light sources, protecting eyes from the Sun, opaque, transparent and translucent materials, making shadows, shadow size, reflected light and light pollution. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Start at lesson 1; a torch is all you need for most practical parts. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What is light?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson introducing light and how we see, with a video and quizzes.
how: A good opener before shadow play with a torch.

title: How can you change the size of a shadow?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on changing a shadow's size; it opens with a starter quiz, then a video and exit quiz.
how: Afterwards let the child move a toy nearer and further from a torch and measure the shadow.

title: Opaque, transparent and translucent
desc: Lesson on sorting materials by how much light passes through them. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Hold glass, butter paper and cardboard up to a window.

title: Protecting our eyes from the Sun
desc: Lesson on why we must never look at the Sun and how to protect our eyes. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Useful before any outdoor shadow or sky activity.

title: Reflected light
desc: Lesson where children investigate light reflecting off surfaces. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Try a mirror, steel plate and cloth with a torch.

title: What is the difference between night and day?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on why we have night and day, with a video and quizzes.
how: Model it with a torch and a ball in a dark room.

title: Rocks and soils (Year 3 unit)
desc: A 16-lesson online unit: rock appearance, hardness, permeability, weathering and erosion, how fossils form, Mary Anning, what soil is made of and a soil permeability practical. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Collect a few stones and a cup of garden soil before starting. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: How is sedimentary rock formed?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson explaining how layers of sediment become sedimentary rock, with a video and quizzes.
how: Shake soil and water in a jar and watch the layers settle.

title: Rock cycle (Year 4 unit)
desc: An Oak online unit on the rock cycle and the different types of rock, with lesson videos and quizzes.
how: Follow on from the Year 3 rocks unit. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: How can we identify different types of rock?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on telling rock types apart by looking at them, with a video and quizzes.
how: Have the child sort stones you collected using what they learn.

title: Physical properties of rocks: hardness
desc: Lesson on testing how hard rocks are, including Mohs' scale. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Scratch test rocks with a fingernail, a coin and a nail, with supervision.

title: Introduction to states of matter and changing states (Year 4 unit)
desc: A 16-lesson online unit: solids, liquids and gases, melting and freezing, using thermometers, evaporation and condensation and the water cycle. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Ice cubes, a pan lid and a thermometer cover most of the practical parts. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What are melting points and boiling points?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on the temperatures at which materials melt and boil, with a video and quizzes.
how: Watch butter, chocolate and ice melt and compare.

title: How do particles behave inside solids, liquids and gases?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on how tiny particles are arranged and move in solids, liquids and gases, with a video and quizzes.
how: Have the child act out particles: standing still, shuffling, then running around.

title: Which mixture makes the best bubbles?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson from a 'mixing and making' unit where children test different mixtures to find which makes the best bubbles.
how: Mix dish soap with water in different amounts and blow bubbles outdoors.

title: How is paper made?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on how paper is made, with a video and quizzes.
how: Follow with making recycled paper from soaked newspaper.

title: Introduction to the human digestive system (Year 4 unit)
desc: A 10-lesson online unit: types of teeth and what they do, teeth of carnivores, herbivores and omnivores, tooth care, and how food travels through the digestive system. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Let the child look at their own teeth in a mirror during the teeth lessons. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: How do humans digest food?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson following food through the digestive system, with a starter quiz, video and exit quiz.
how: Trace the path on a drawn body outline afterwards.

title: Are all teeth the same?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson comparing the different kinds of teeth and their jobs, with a video and quizzes.
how: Ask which teeth bite a guava and which chew it.

title: Types of teeth
desc: Lesson on incisors, canines and molars. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Print the worksheet to label after the pupil lesson.

title: Earth, Sun and Moon (Year 5 unit)
desc: A 12-lesson online unit: the shape of Earth, observing the Moon, sizes of Earth, Sun and Moon, day and night, the Sun's apparent movement, the planets and how they move. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Pair with a Moon diary kept over a month. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What is space?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson introducing space and what is in it, with a video and quizzes.
how: A good first lesson before the Earth, Sun and Moon unit.

title: Why the Sun appears to move across the sky
desc: Lesson explaining that the Sun seems to move because the Earth spins. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Mark a stick's shadow in the yard at three times of day.

title: The planets in our solar system
desc: Lesson on the eight planets and their order from the Sun. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Make a planet line-up with fruit of different sizes.

title: The shape of Earth
desc: Lesson on the evidence that the Earth is a sphere. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Look at a globe together after the lesson.

title: How we see the Moon from Earth
desc: Lesson on why the Moon's shape seems to change. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Model Moon phases with a ball and a lamp.

title: Forces including simple machines (Year 5 unit)
desc: A 13-lesson online unit: gravity, pushes and pulls, friction, air and water resistance investigations, and how levers, pulleys and gears help us. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Start with 'Introduction to gravity'; the friction and resistance lessons have plan-do-review practicals. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: Friction: plan an investigation
desc: Lesson where children plan a fair test of friction on different surfaces. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Slide a toy car down a tilted board covered with cloth, paper and foil.

title: Which factors affect an object's ability to float?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson investigating what makes objects float or sink, with a video and quizzes.
how: Test a bucket of water with objects of different shapes and materials.

title: Evolution and inheritance (Year 6 unit)
desc: A 14-lesson online unit: what fossils tell us, how living things changed over time, human skulls, offspring that are similar but not identical, inherited characteristics, adaptations, Darwin's finches and survival of the fittest. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Do the 'offspring' and 'family trees' lessons with family photos. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What is the theory of evolution?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson introducing the theory of evolution, with a video and quizzes.
how: Use with older children after the fossils lessons.

title: Family trees
desc: Lesson on drawing family trees and seeing how features pass down generations. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Have the child draw your own family tree and note who shares which features.

title: Charles Darwin and finches
desc: Lesson on how Darwin noticed finches' beaks suited their food. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Compare beaks of birds you see locally: crow, sparrow, kingfisher.

title: Introduction to the human skeleton and muscles (Year 3 unit)
desc: A 10-lesson online unit on how the skeleton supports and protects us, bone length, animal skeletons, animals without bones and muscles for movement. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Let the child feel their own ribs, skull and elbow joint as you go. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: The human skeleton: protection
desc: Lesson on how bones like the skull and ribs protect organs. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Ask what the skull and ribs are guarding.

title: Animals without bones
desc: Lesson on animals with no bony skeleton, such as worms and insects. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Look for earthworms and snails in the garden after rain.

title: Plants (Year 3 unit)
desc: A six-lesson online unit on plant parts, what plants need to grow and how plants are adapted, with lesson videos and quizzes.
how: Grow a bean or methi in two pots, one in the dark, alongside it. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: The function of leaves
desc: Lesson on what leaves do for a plant. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Collect different leaves on a walk to look at before the worksheet.

title: Structure of a flowering plant
desc: Year 1 lesson on naming the parts of a flowering plant: roots, stem, leaves, flower. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Pull up a weed and label its real parts.

title: Structure of a tree
desc: Year 1 lesson on the parts of a tree: trunk, branches, roots, leaves. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Hug a tree in the park and name its parts together.

title: Deciduous and evergreen trees
desc: Year 1 lesson on trees that lose their leaves and trees that keep them. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Notice which trees near you drop leaves before summer.

title: Wildflowers
desc: Year 1 lesson on spotting and naming wild flowering plants. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Take a walk and photograph wild flowers growing in cracks and verges.

title: What plants need to grow and stay healthy
desc: Year 2 lesson on plants' needs for water, light and a suitable temperature. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Set up pots with and without water and compare over a week.

title: Living or non-living
desc: Year 2 lesson on sorting things into living, dead and never alive. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Sort objects from around the house and garden into three piles.

title: Animal habitats
desc: Year 2 lesson on how habitats give animals what they need. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Talk about where pigeons, ants and fish live and why.

title: Plants and animals in microhabitats
desc: Year 2 lesson on tiny habitats like under a log or stone and what lives there. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Lift a flowerpot or stone in the garden and look at what lives under it.

title: Protecting microhabitats
desc: Year 2 lesson on caring for small habitats and the creatures in them. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Afterwards, put back any stones you lifted and leave a corner of the garden wild.

title: Human body parts (Year 1 unit)
desc: Overview of a six-lesson Year 1 unit: humans are animals, body parts on the outside and inside, body parts for our senses, and more about sight, smell, sound, taste and touch.
how: Use it to plan the order, then open each lesson's pupil video.

title: Body parts for our senses
desc: An Oak Year 1 pupil video linking eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin to the five senses.
how: Play 'point to the part' afterwards.

title: More about sight, smell and sound
desc: An Oak Year 1 pupil video looking more closely at the senses of sight, smell and hearing.
how: Do a smell-guessing game with spices from the kitchen.

title: Seasonal changes: spring and summer (Year 1 unit)
desc: A five-lesson online unit: signs of spring, weather in spring, signs of summer, weather in summer and day length in summer. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Seasons in India differ from the UK, so compare with your local monsoon and winter. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: Day length in winter
desc: Year 1 lesson on how days are shorter in winter. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Note sunrise and sunset times for a week in December and in June.

title: What is hibernation?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson about animals that sleep through the cold season, with a video and quizzes.
how: Talk about which animals in the Himalayas hibernate.

title: How do trees change across the seasons?
desc: KS1 lesson on how trees look different in each season. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Photograph one tree near home every month.

title: Everyday materials (Year 1 unit)
desc: A nine-lesson online unit: objects and the materials they are made of, recycling and the 3 Rs, material properties, waterproof materials and transparent and opaque materials. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Go on a 'what is it made of?' hunt around the house. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: What is a material?
desc: An Oak pupil video on the difference between an object and the material it is made of, like wood, plastic and metal.
how: Ask the child to name the material of five things on the table.

title: Which materials are absorbent?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson testing which materials soak up water, with a video and quizzes.
how: Drip water onto a towel, newspaper, plastic and foil to compare.

title: The 3 Rs
desc: Year 1 lesson on reduce, reuse and recycle. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Set up a sorting box for dry waste at home.

title: Micro-organisms are living things
desc: Year 6 lesson showing that tiny micro-organisms are living things too. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Follow with watching bread go mouldy in a sealed bag.

title: Microorganisms that help us
desc: Year 6 lesson on useful microbes, such as those in yeast and yoghurt. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Make curd at home and talk about the bacteria doing the work.

title: Grouping micro-organisms
desc: Year 6 lesson on sorting micro-organisms into groups such as bacteria and fungi. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Use after the 'micro-organisms are living things' lesson.

title: What are the different animal kingdoms?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on how living things are grouped into kingdoms, with a video and quizzes.
how: Have the child sort picture cards of living things afterwards.

title: Reproduction and life cycles: plants (Year 5 unit)
desc: A nine-lesson online unit: parts of a flowering plant, pollinators, asexual reproduction and cuttings, plant life cycles, selective breeding and seed banks. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Grow a money plant from a cutting alongside the lessons. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: Reproduction and life cycles: animals (Year 5 unit)
desc: An 11-lesson online unit: animal groups, insects, and the life cycles of mammals, birds and amphibians compared. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Watch for tadpoles in monsoon puddles to link to the amphibian lesson. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: Why do plants have flowers?
desc: An Oak pupil lesson on what flowers do for a plant, including pollination, with a video and quizzes.
how: Look at a hibiscus flower and find its parts.

title: Asexual reproduction in plants
desc: Year 5 lesson on plants that grow new plants without seeds, such as from runners or bulbs. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Put a potato or onion in water and watch it sprout.

title: Healthy eating (Year 3 unit)
desc: A 12-lesson online unit: types of food, nutrition from food, fats in food, different diets for different people, planning a nutrient-rich meal and sustainable and local food. The unit page lists the lessons in order; each lesson has a short video, a starter quiz and an exit quiz the child works through online.
how: Link each lesson to your own thali: dal, roti, sabzi, curd. Some older Oak lessons are being replaced by newer versions, so if a page has moved, look for the newer one on Oak.

title: Types of food
desc: Year 3 lesson on sorting food into groups. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Sort the week's groceries into food groups.

title: Local food
desc: Year 3 lesson on where food comes from and why eating local food helps the environment. A teacher lesson page where you download free slides, a worksheet and quizzes for the lesson.
how: Visit a local sabzi market and ask where the produce was grown.

title: Grade 2 Plants Science Worksheets
desc: Printable worksheets on what plants need, photosynthesis, seeds and seed dispersal, pollination, the plant life cycle and plant habitats, with answers on a second page.
how: Read the page before printing: some worksheets are free, while downloadable packs cost a little.

title: Grade 2 Science Worksheets
desc: The index of K5 Learning's grade 2 science worksheets, sorted by topic, each printable with an answer sheet.
how: Pick a topic that matches this week's lesson; some printable packs cost a small fee.
